newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Trans Hex Namibia diamond prospect bright.
newsitem.headline: Trans Hex Namibia diamond prospect bright.

text.p: Canada's Trans Hex International Ltd said on Friday it had achieved promising drilling results at its Namibian diamond prospects.

"(Trans Hex) is pleased to announce that significant progress has been made in the drill definition of the diamondiferous gravel bodies located in ancient paleochannels on the property," the company said in a statement.
The drilling results refer to Block 9, Namibia.
Drilling began in April and about 75 percent of the area has been drilled to date with completion scheduled for December 1996, the company said.
Trans Hex said that similar gravel bodies in the area had surrendered diamonds of above average value, in excess of US$500 per carat.

To date about C$600,000 had been spent on the acquisition and exploration of the property. A further C$700,000 has been budgeted to end-March 1997 to complete the drilling and initiate the bulk sampling programme.
Three-quarters of these amounts have been or will be funded by Trans Hex International Ltd in terms of the joint venture agreement.

The joint venture is operated through Namibia's Northbank Diamonds Ltd, 50 percent owned by Trans Hex International, 30 percent by Lazare Kaplan International Ltd and 20 percent by Stocks & Stocks (Namibia) Mining (Pty) Ltd.
